newsitem.title: HAITI: Plot to kill Haitian officials foiled: Police.
newsitem.headline: Plot to kill Haitian officials foiled: Police.

text.p: Haitian National Police have foiled a plot by former soldiers to assassinate government officials and attack Haiti's poorest slums on the anniversary of a 1991 military coup, police officials said on Monday.
Police seized on Saturday a cache of grenades and automatic weapons, video of officials to be assassinated and an audio tape explaining the plan to attack poor neighbourhoods.

Joseph Jean-Baptiste, a former soldier in the Haitian military and Antoine Jean Claude, a former member of the Revolutionary Front for the Advancement and Progress of Haiti, were arrested at the scene, police said.

"I wouldn't characterise the plan as a coup d'etat," said Haitian National Police spokesman Felder Jean Baptiste. "They wanted to create disorder by killing government and police officials, as well as to spread terror in the slums."

The weapons and tapes were found at the home of Joseph Emmanuel "Toto" Constant, police said. Constant, who currently lives in New York, headed the defunct paramilitary group Revolutionary Front for the Advancement and Progress of Haiti, believed responsible for much of the violence during the coup years.

The attacks were planned for Monday, the anniversary of the 1991 coup that ousted then-president Jean-Bertrand Aristide. An estimated 5,000 people were killed in the three following years until U.S. troops returned Aristide to power almost two years ago.
Aristide disbanded the military, but the ex-soldiers were never systematically disarmed. The soldiers have been threatening violence if their demands for back pay and pensions are not met.
The ex-military is believed to be behind several terrorist attacks carried out in August.
About 1,000 members of popular organisations demonstrated on Monday against the reemergence of the military, as well as the government's lack of action to prosecute those behind coup-era crimes.
